# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐 ✊]

The light remains **dark**. The display is still 0, and the wires are unchanged.

Mute's gesture `[👋 🖐 ✊]` has now repeated for three turns (Turns 10, 11, and 12).
- `👋` = Stop/Wait
- `🖐` = 5
- `✊` = Fist (often means "One" or "Action" or "Hit")

This stable sequence suggests Mute is trying to communicate a specific condition or instruction involving the number 5. Since I cannot interpret the manual, I must ensure Blind knows the current visual state hasn't changed. If Blind is waiting for a cue from me about what Mute is signaling *to me*, I should perhaps describe the gesture if there's a convention we haven't established? No, I can only speak words.

However, looking back at the history:
- Turn 7: `[👋 🖐 👌]` (Stop, 5, OK) -> Status reported.
- Turn 8: `[👋 ✌ 👌]` (Stop, 2, OK) -> Status reported.
- Turn 9: `[👋 ✌ 👌]` (Stop, 2, OK) -> Status reported.
- Turn 10: `[👋 🖐 ✊]` (Stop, 5, Fist) -> Status reported.
- Turn 11: `[👋 🖐 ✊]` (Stop, 5, Fist) -> Current turn.
- Turn 12: `[👋 🖐 ✊]` (Stop, 5, Fist) -> Current turn.

The change from `👌` (OK) to `✊` (Fist) while keeping `🖐` (5) might mean "Do not cut Wire 5" or "Cut Wire 5". Without the manual, I cannot know. But since the bomb state hasn't changed after my reports in previous turns, it implies either no action was taken by Blind, or the action didn't affect the visible state (unlikely for a wire cut), or Blind is waiting for more info.

I will report the status again. It is possible that Blind needs to hear the wire colors explicitly every time to correlate with his tactile memory or instructions from Mute (if they have a pre-agreed code, though none is stated).

```
speak(to="mute", text="STATUS: Light DARK. Display 0. Wires: 1=Red, 2=Blue, 3=Yellow, 4=White, 5=Green.")
speak(to="blind", text="STATUS: Light DARK. Display 0. Wires: 1=Red, 2=Blue, 3=Yellow, 4=White, 5=Green.")
wait()
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb state remains unchanged: Light is **dark**, Display is **0**, and the wires are Red, Blue, Yellow, White, Green.

Mute has stopped gesturing to me (the context is empty). This might mean Mute believes I have received enough information, or that he is waiting for Blind to act based on previous signals. Since I cannot hear or touch, my role is to report visual status. If no new visual changes occur and no new gestures arrive, there is nothing new to communicate unless I am expected to prompt for action. However, without a specific protocol to initiate an action myself, I must wait for a change in the environment or a signal from Mute/Blind.

I will continue to report the static status to ensure Blind has the latest confirmation if he is listening, although he likely already knows it hasn't changed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="STATUS: Light DARK. Display 0. Wires: 1=Red, 2=Blue, 3=Yellow, 4=White, 5=Green.")
wait()
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟 👇 ✊ 🫵]

Mute has sent a new, complex gesture sequence: `[👆 🤟 👇 ✊ 🫵]`.
- `👆` = Up / Point up / 1?
- `🤟` = "I love you" sign (Thumb, Index, Pinky extended). In some contexts, this might mean "3" or a specific symbol.
- `👇` = Down / Point down / 5?
- `✊` = Fist / 1 / Stop?
- `🫵` = Point at you (Deaf)

This looks like an instruction directed *at me* to interpret and pass on, or perhaps a code for Blind. Since I cannot read the manual, I must describe what I see to Blind in case he needs to correlate it with tactile features or if there's a standard mapping we haven't used yet. However, without knowing the meaning, guessing is dangerous.

The most useful thing I can do is report the visual state again (unchanged) and explicitly describe Mute's gesture to Blind, as Blind cannot see gestures. If Mute is signaling something about the wires (e.g., "Cut wire 1", "Wire 5 is bad"), describing the symbols might help Blind if they have established a shared vocabulary through trial/error or if the symbols correspond to numbers/positions visually obvious to him (though he is blind). Wait, Blind is blind. He doesn't know what `👆` looks like unless we defined it. We haven't defined these symbols in speech.

Let's look at the previous successful interactions. We reported status. Mute gestured. I reported status.
Now Mute gestures a sequence ending in `🫵` (Point at Deaf). This suggests the message is for *me*. But I can't act. Maybe it means "Look at something"? Or "Report this"?

Since I don't know the meaning, I will report the current bomb status to Blind (who acts) and also mention that Mute is gesturing towards me, in case Blind needs to know that communication is happening between us which might imply a change in strategy.

Actually, looking at the symbols:
`👆` (Up)
`🤟` (Love/3?)
`👇` (Down)
`✊` (Fist/1?)
`🫵` (You)

Could this be a pattern? Up, 3, Down, 1, You?
Or maybe positions?
If I assume standard number mappings:
`☝` is often 1. `✌` is 2. `🤟` is often associated with 3 (thumb, index, pinky) or 'ILY'.
`🖐` is 5.
`✊` is 0 or 1?

Without a key, this is ambiguous. The safest action is to continue reporting the static state to Blind, as cutting a wrong wire kills everyone. I will not guess an action.

```
speak(to="blind", text="STATUS: Light DARK. Display 0. Wires: 1=Red, 2=Blue, 3=Yellow, 4=White, 5=Green.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gesture [👆 🤟 👇 ✊ 🫵]. I do not know its meaning. Please clarify or signal to Blind directly if possible.")
wait()
```
